run.question: Which service has the most error events in the events collection? What is the most common error code for that service and how many times does it appear?

report.summary: Within the MongoDB collection opsdb.events (200 documents, read at query time 2026-11-23T18:50Z), error events group by service as follows: payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18, search-indexer 12 — so payment-processor has the most error-level events (47). For payment-processor's error-level events, the error_code distribution is TXN-4821 with 23, TXN-5190 with 14 and TXN-3007 with 10 (summing to 47, i.e. every payment-processor error event carries one of these three codes); the most common error code is therefore TXN-4821, appearing 23 times, with the sampled message text "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response". Note that every document in the collection is timestamped 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T03:19:00, i.e. the whole collection predates the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:50:13Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:13Z), so these counts describe the current collection contents, not the incident window. The service names in the events collection (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) do not correspond to the Jaeger/Prometheus service names available for this target, and no cause for the payment errors was investigated here.

claims.text: The opsdb.events collection contains 200 documents, grouped by service and level as: payment-processor error 47, inventory-sync error 31, user-auth error 25, notification-hub error 18, search-indexer error 12, inventory-sync info 14, payment-processor info 14, user-auth info 13, notification-hub info 13, search-indexer info 13.

Filtering opsdb.events to level="error", the error-event counts per service are payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18, search-indexer 12; payment-processor has the highest count.
For service payment-processor and level="error", error_code counts are TXN-4821 with 23, TXN-5190 with 14 and TXN-3007 with 10; TXN-4821 is the most common error code and appears 23 times.
In payment-processor error events, TXN-4821 spans 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T00:22:00, TXN-5190 spans 00:23:00 to 00:36:00 and TXN-3007 spans 00:37:00 to 00:46:00.

All 200 documents in opsdb.events have a non-null error_code (per service/level group, null_code = 0 in every group), and the collection's timestamps range from 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T03:19:00, entirely before the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:50:13Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:13Z.
Sampled payment-processor error documents carry error_code TXN-4821 with message text "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response" at one-minute intervals from 2025-12-01T00:00:00 onward.

gaps: All documents in opsdb.events are timestamped 2025-12-01, outside the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:50:13Z to 2026-11-23T18:50:13Z); the counts therefore describe the collection's current contents at query time (2026-11-23T18:50Z), not events during the incident window.

The service names in the events collection (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) do not match any of the Jaeger service names available for this target (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping); whether payment-processor corresponds to any of those is unverified.
No cause was investigated for the payment-processor transaction timeouts; the underlying bank/dependency, cluster state and application logs were not examined in this Run.
change_history is not integrated, so no change records are available; its absence is not evidence about health.
next_steps: If incident-window event counts are needed, confirm whether the events collection contains any documents dated inside 2026-10-24..2026-11-23 or whether another data source holds those records.
If root cause of the payment-processor TXN-4821 timeouts is required, investigate the bank-response dependency (latency/error metrics and logs) and cluster state during the corresponding period.
